newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Third group to challenge ruling on Argentine post.
newsitem.headline: Third group to challenge ruling on Argentine post.

text.p: A Brazilian-headed group, said Wednesday it too will challenge an official ruling that it did not qualify to bid on the concession to run Argentine postal firm ENCOTESA.
"We will challenge (the decision)," Jose Chalen, representative of the group headed by Brazilian airline VASP, told Reuters. The group is the third consortium to appeal the ruling.
A commission handling the awarding of ENCOTESA's 30-year concession said last week the group failed to present a detailed investment plan.
But Chalen said it will challenge the ruling by the end of today, the deadline for appeals, as "we believe ... the plan the commission refers to is expressly mentioned in the documents we presented.
"Then, we also consider that in case there was an omission, the commission should have asked that the data be completed, as stated in the conditions for the concession".

The group is formed by VASP, with a 60 percent holding, local firm Brazal with 20 percent, Argentine Banco del Chubut with 10 percent and local postal firm Andreani, also with 10 percent. It proposed Italy's post office as operator.
A Dutch group headed by ING Barings and local building firm Roggio had already said they will challenge the ruling.
Challengers must deposit $500,000, which will be reimbursed if the appeal is won.
Three other consortia have qualified for the concession.

The commission has said it will answer the challenges in time for a "data room" that will be opened July 1. This is a month-long period when bidders are granted wider information on ENCOTESA. ((-- Guillermo Haskel, Buenos Aires Newsroom, 541 318-0650))
